title: Serialize and Deserialize Binary Tree
summary: Turn a binary tree into a string and rebuild the identical tree from that string.

tests.explain: Whatever string you invent, deserializing it must rebuild this exact tree (shape and values).
An empty tree must serialize to some string and come back as an empty tree.

hints: A traversal that lists only the values loses the shape. What extra information must the string record so that the shape can be rebuilt?
Record the missing children too: write a marker such as # for every null child. A preorder or level-order listing with null markers describes exactly one tree.

Serialize with a level-order BFS, writing each value or the marker, joined by commas. To deserialize, split the string, create the root, and walk the tokens with a queue of parents: the next two tokens are the left and right child of the node you pop.

complexity.time: O(n) for both serialize and deserialize
complexity.space: O(n) for the string and the queue
